event: Wren tells Theron before breakfast, throwing away the speech she rehearsed.
She sees his scarred hands on his cup and his glance south-east.
She tells him: Rimfolk stonework with guild marks, a settlement, ruins.
His hands go still: something very old touched for the first time.
She admits she kept it overnight and says she is sorry.
His grandmother said there were buildings in the basin; three generations never looked.
'You kept it one night because you wanted it yours before it was mine.' 'Yes.'
His grandmother said the first hour of knowing is sweetest; the showing is better.
He takes his gathering knife and coat. 'Show me.'
Hadley comes out already laced, notebook in hand, ready to sketch guild marks.
Wren leads south-east by [Trail Memory]; the sweetness is deeper today.
The network hums with the Shelf's warming stone and the Eye's still surface.
Theron walks ahead in silence, toward what he spent a lifetime not walking toward.
They cross the grove's corruption boundary; Theron knows it by feel.
Wren's foot finds the first stone. 'Here.'
In daylight the ruins are larger: a ring of foundations around a central hall.
Behind the ring, stone-walled garden terraces climb a rise.
The bond-potentials are a chorus now; one deep, clean pull beats at the center.
'The well,' Theron says: the well at the center, the houses in a ring.
He crouches at a wall and traces a guild mark. 'This is a Wynn mark.'
Hadley's breath catches: his family's mark. The next is Blackroot.
At the hall Theron reads Osk, Brenn, Ashvale, Holt, then rests his palm on the stone.
Wren does not map; she watches him, and staying still is the hardest thing she has done.
Hadley holds his notebook unwritten: 'My grandmother said we came from the south.'
Theron walks the settlement alone for twenty minutes while they wait at its edge.
Wren feels fifteen or more potentials; the hall is loudest, the well cleanest.
She realizes his south-east glance has always pointed here.
He returns with a small carved stone from the hall's fire-blackened hearth.
'Survey it. My grandmother would have wanted it mapped.' 'We'll survey together.'
'The well first. The well is the heart.'
The limestone well is clear, its water three meters down, bright and still.
The water comes from below the corruption's reach; the well remembered what the forest forgot.
Wren touches the warm rim, and does not bond it: understanding matters more than speed.
A discovery logs the central well, bond potential high: +45 XP.

changes.note: Discovery: Varethen central well, high bond potential

event: For three hours they survey: Theron leads from memory, Hadley sketches, six marks confirmed.
They find the doorway his grandmother described, worn smooth on one side.
The terrace soil is fine and dark with centuries of cultivation.
Theron names the Roothold: the great settlement in the deep basin that the corruption took.
This settlement is a daughter community, built the Roothold's way.
A discovery logs the garden terraces in the Roothold tradition: +35 XP.

changes.note: Discovery: Varethen garden terraces, Roothold tradition

event: At the hall's entrance the threshold stone under her boot radiates warmth.
She has stood on it forty minutes, and it has been receiving her attention.
[Lay the Path] opens; this time she did not reach, the bond came to her.
The stone's welcome is worn into it by every foot that entered the hall.
The bond seats below the others, a foundation, like roots of her own.
BOND FORMED: Varethen Threshold Stone, [Dormant], Cluster Anchor; Slot 2 unlocks; +50 XP.

changes.note: Sympathetic Bond formed: Varethen threshold stone, cluster anchor

event: Shelf is shelter, Eye is clarity, the threshold stone is patience.
At the north-east edge she finds ghost elms planted in a deliberate arc.
'Theron, these trees were planted.' 'Yes.' The resonance was used as a ward.
Seventy meters along, one ghost elm is dead: a gap in the ward.
Corruption seeps through the gap; the buildings inside it feel damaged.
The Shelf flinches in her chest and the Eye dims: her places are afraid.
She steps back inside the ward until the bonds ease and her hands stop shaking.
At the well, between two pen strokes, she reaches Level 4.

changes.note: Level 4 reached during the Varethen survey

event: Compass Sensitivity tier 2: the needle reads bond strength, and drags at corruption.
She sweeps the compass: the settlement is clean; the drag sits at the gap's bearing.
She is learning to read the land's health through her father's tool.
They eat at the well: Theron's cold flatcakes, Hadley's berries and root cake.
Theron names the scattered families: Wynn in Millhaven, Osk at the escarpment, his aunt Maret.
Hadley's Millhaven run is in four days; Wren asks him to carry word to Maret.
'This isn't mine to keep,' Wren tells Theron. 'It was never mine.'
Theron nods once: 'Tell her the well is clean. Tell her Theron says come.'
They walk back in the late afternoon; the compass reads pulls and absences.
A hundred meters from camp Wren stops: 'The stream. It moved.'
The deadfall is gone; the stream is wider, tidied, six feet closer to her camp.
Hadley finds the bank firm: this soil does not shift overnight.
The water smells faintly sweet; the compass needle flutters, undecided.
A garbled notification: the water was directed to her. 'Please stay.'
She pulls her hand from the water: the corruption has noticed her.
It rearranged the stream to impress her: the corruption is courting her.
'Your face is doing a thing.' She says something is speaking through the System.
Theron, hand on his knife, asks what it said. 'Please stay.'
His grandmother said: if the forest starts wanting you, walk the other way.
The Thornwild is mapping her back.
She sleeps badly, the stream running close and sweet in the dark.
She feels the Shelf steady, the Eye watchful, the ruins waiting north-east.
The corruption doesn't want to hurt her; it wants to be her only bond.
She does not drink from the stream; she sleeps with the compass in her hand.
The Crying Forest is fourteen days from its next event; she is counting.
